In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
knowledge sharing and learning is a very complicated phenomenon and that it is not easy to identify the conditions for'success' in knowledge sharing and learning.

the conditions for successful alliance knowledge sharing are: (1) the presence of a 'common ground', (2) a'shared vision', (3) a'shared identity', (4) 'openness' and (5) a'safe environment' for knowledge sharing.
the conditions for knowledge sharing and learning are complex and that the conditions at the inter-personal and inter-organisitional level are inter-related.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
'successful' knowledge transfer and learning in inter-firm alliances is a function of the combination of both the inter-personal and inter-organisional conditions.
the inter-organizational level and the interpersonal level are equally important for successful knowledge sharing in alliances.

knowledge sharing and learning are facilitated when: 1) the knowledge is of a tacit nature; 2) the knowledge is not easily available in the environment; 3) the knowledge is complementary to existing knowledge of the partners; 4) the knowledge is important for the alliance; 5) the knowledge is shared in a 'trustful' way; 6) there are no strong differences in knowledge between partners; 7) the alliance is not too complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in alliances where competing companies co-operate, the inter-personal level is important in addition to the inter-organizational level.
the inter-personal relations between individuals in the alliance are of great importance for the'success' of the alliance.
the conditions for knowledge sharing and learning can only be fully understood when both the inter-organizational and the inter-personal level are taken into account.
